bottleneck: Real BF16 C128 DECODE trace (Controller packet, GB10 a1, 16 forwards, bs=128, Medium512/64, frozen launch with --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64): per-step GPU time 35.33 ms splits into attention 16.68 ms (47.5 %), GEMM+lm_head 16.96 ms (48.3 %), sampling 0.39 ms (1.1 %), other 1.11 ms (3.2 %). The host is fully hidden: kernel union is 99.25 % of the 16 GPU step windows, CPU step work is 1.68 ms/step, and 99.44 % of cudaEventSynchronize time is nested inside kernel execution. Every step is a CUDA-graph replay (16/16 cudaGraphLaunch) despite the frozen max-bs-64 CLI, confirming the memory_hook RSI widening hook is already active in this measured tree. The remaining question this iteration answers is whether the dominant attention cost scales with cached context as a KV-byte roofline would require.
hypothesis: H1 (activation): the 16 observed C128 decode steps replay captured graphs and have no host-side critical path. H2 (new falsifier): if per-step attention time were proportional to KV bytes, each decode step appends one position per request, so attention time must rise by mean_attn/513 = +0.0325 ms/step over the capture; a measured slope statistically below that rejects KV-byte proportionality over this window and implies a context-independent scheduling/grid term dominates. EXECUTED RESULT: H1 confirmed (16/16 graph launches; min step kernel-union fraction 0.9672, steps 1-15 >= 0.9922; event-sync nested fraction 0.9944). H2 falsified as stated: OLS slope -0.00344 +/- 0.00413 ms/step (about 8.9 standard errors below the +0.0325 prediction; ratio -0.106), attention 16.57-16.85 ms across +15 KV positions per request. Therefore KV-byte reduction is not evidenced as a lever at this operating point, and host/sync/launch changes cannot move it.
patch: No engine change. Analysis-only iteration: g3-t13/analyze_decode_trace.py (stdlib gzip/json, python3 -I) reads the Controller trace read-only and emits g3-t13/raw/decode_trace_analysis.json + g3-t13/raw/analyze_stdout.txt. Hard preconditions (16 launches, 16 CPU labels, 16 GPU step spans, kernel count multiple of 16) fail closed with exit 2; step windows come from GPU step annotations, not from asynchronous host launch timestamps (a first attempt using launch timestamps produced boundary artifacts and was discarded before commit). Originals untouched; trace sha256 pinned.
tests: EXECUTED (CPU, stdlib only): python3 -I g3-t13/analyze_decode_trace.py controller_evidence/continuous-20261109-01/20261110-decode-trace/decode.trace.json.gz --out g3-t13/raw/decode_trace_analysis.json -> exit 0, verdict HOST_HIDDEN_GRAPH_REPLAY_EVERY_STEP. Checks: 8560 kernel events, 16 cudaGraphLaunch, 16 CPU and 16 GPU step[DECODE bs=128] spans, 529 kernels/step; kernel union 35.024/35.334 ms per step mean; attention 448 calls = 28/step; lm_head GEMM 16 calls = 1/step at 2.59 ms implies ~31 TFLOPS at 128x~152k x2048 BF16 (compute-roofline). Falsifier F2 (min union >= 0.95) and F3 (event-sync nested >= 0.95) both pass; H2's KV-proportional slope prediction fails. REQUESTED (bounded custom diagnostic, not a fast gate, request_fast_gate=false): after the next ordinary BF16 diagnostic, capture one decode-only torch profile each at bs=32 and bs=128 with an identical prompt/context length (same frozen launch, e.g. Medium 512/64 at C32 and C128), and record per step the same fields already proven collectable in this packet (cudaGraphLaunch ts, GPU step[DECODE bs=N] span, kernel union, attention summed ms, kernel count). Expected discriminator pre-registered from this packet: if attention time is ~constant across bs (fixed scheduling floor), C32 attention/step would be much closer to 16.7 ms than to 16.7*(32/128)=4.2 ms; if it scales with batch, it follows the 4.2 ms line. Either outcome decides whether attention cost is per-step-fixed or throughput-bound at this context. Bounds: 2 short traces, no scoring, no speed claim, no numeric/quality claim; trace perturbs timing so only within-trace per-step structure is compared, never wall-clock ratios.
learning: The real C128 decode trace shows no host headroom and a context-flat attention component. This is consistent with (does not prove) a per-step scheduling/parallelism floor in flashinfer tensor-core decode at bs=128, and it blocks two assumptions: (1) that sync/launch/host optimizations can raise this point, and (2) that KV-byte reduction (FP8 KV, cache pruning) would speed C128 at ~513-528 context. The absolute attention level remains 47.5 % of the step, and GEMM+lm_head is a further 48.3 % already near BF16 peak, so no BF16-safe candidate is proposed from this evidence. The trial-1 graph-widening hook is verified active in the measured tree and cannot be re-claimed. Limits: 16 consecutive steps of one instrumented run, one batch size, one prompt length, no SM counters, trace may perturb races/timings, original diagnostic INCONCLUSIVE; kernel union is not SM utilization.
next_proposal: Run the two-trace bs scaling diagnostic above (C32 vs C128, identical context) to separate a per-step fixed attention floor from batch-linear attention cost. Decision tree: (a) attention ~constant across bs -> the cost is a fixed per-step structure (grid/split/merge); next inspect the flashinfer decode wrapper plan (split-KV tile size, merge kernel) with a CPU-side selection oracle and only then propose a candidate, keeping numerics/quality open. (b) attention scales ~linearly with bs -> decode is throughput-bound, concurrency-level changes are the right lever and a BF16 Fast screen of a scheduling-side candidate is justified. Do not re-propose graph widening (already active, verified here) and do not request FP8 KV promotion on the basis of this trace. If the controller opens the NGRAM lane instead, the previously requested bounded per-step accept/trace instrumentation remains the priority there; F1 stays BUG_CONFIRMED either way.
uncertainty: UNRESOLVED_MECHANISM: the context-independent attention term is inferred from a flat marginal slope over 16 steps (+15 positions/request on ~513) of a single instrumented run; it does not establish the absolute cost at other context lengths, batch sizes, or nodes, and trace instrumentation may perturb scheduling. No train-step, SM, or bandwidth counters are present, so 'fixed scheduling floor' is a hypothesis compatible with the data, not a measurement of its cause. No speedup, EXACT, quality, gate or promotion claim is made; F1/F2 remain open.
